# Story 17.1: Red-phase unit tests for CSRF token comparison and session-id derivation

Status: in-progress

## Story

As a developer,
I want red-phase unit tests asserting the presented CSRF token is compared to the stored token in constant time and that `sessionId` derives from an unguessable server-issued value,
So that Story 17.2 has a defined, executable contract to make pass when it closes the CSRF comparison gap (P0 item #4 from Aspect 9 of the critical review).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A spec asserts that `validateStoredToken` in `apps/server/src/app/middleware/validate-csrf-token.function.ts` compares the presented token against `storedData.token` — a request with only a live (unexpired) stored entry but a WRONG or ABSENT presented token is REJECTED, not passed.
2. A spec asserts the comparison is constant-time (e.g., uses `crypto.timingSafeEqual` or an equivalent), so timing does not leak whether the prefix matched.
3. A spec asserts that `sessionId` no longer derives from client-supplied `ip`/`userAgent`/minute — it comes from an unguessable server-issued value instead of `sha256(ip-userAgent-minute)`.
4. All assertions in AC #1–#3 are marked `.skip()` (`it.skip`) so the server Vitest suite runs green BEFORE Story 17.2 exists — red-phase by skip, not by failure. Existing passing tests remain unskipped and green.
5. The spec file(s) run green under `nx test server` immediately after this story (new red-phase tests skipped), and Story 17.2's first task is to remove the `.skip()` markers, confirm they FAIL against current code, then implement until they pass.

## Tasks / Subtasks

- [ ] Task 1 (AC: #1): Add a mismatched/absent-token rejection assertion.
  - [ ] 1.1 In `apps/server/src/app/middleware/validate-csrf-token.function.spec.ts`, assert that with a live unexpired stored entry, a request presenting the WRONG token is rejected, and a request presenting NO token is also rejected.
- [ ] Task 2 (AC: #2): Add a constant-time comparison assertion.
  - [ ] 2.1 Assert the presented-vs-stored comparison uses a constant-time primitive (`crypto.timingSafeEqual` or equivalent) rather than `===`.
- [ ] Task 3 (AC: #3): Add an unguessable session-id derivation assertion.
  - [ ] 3.1 In `apps/server/src/app/utils/generate-session-id.function.spec.ts`, assert the derived `sessionId` does not depend on client-supplied `ip`/`userAgent`/minute — i.e., it comes from a server-issued unguessable value (e.g., `crypto.randomUUID()` / `randomBytes`).
- [ ] Task 4 (AC: #4, #5): Mark red-phase assertions `.skip()` and confirm green.
  - [ ] 4.1 Apply `it.skip` to every assertion added in Tasks 1–3 — they are red until Story 17.2 fixes the comparison + derivation. Leave all pre-existing tests unskipped.
  - [ ] 4.2 Run `nx test server` and confirm fully green with only the new red-phase tests skipped. Do NOT weaken or delete any assertion to achieve this — skip markers only.

## Dev Notes

- **Why:** `validateStoredToken` in `apps/server/src/app/middleware/validate-csrf-token.function.ts` (lines ~119–142) never compares the presented token to the stored one — it only checks an entry exists and is unexpired, so any request with a live entry passes. Separately, `generate-session-id.function.ts:4-13` derives `sessionId` from `sha256(ip-userAgent-minute)`, which is guessable/collidable. This is P0 item #4 from Aspect 9.
- **Red-phase TDD:** this story is ordered before Story 17.2. Assertions are marked `it.skip` so CI stays green while the gap still exists; Story 17.2's first task removes the skip markers, confirms red, then fixes until green.
- **Do NOT modify production code in this story** — unit-test scaffold only. The fix belongs to Story 17.2.
- Vitest is the workspace test framework; server tests run via `nx test server`.

### Project Structure Notes

- Create/modify: `apps/server/src/app/middleware/validate-csrf-token.function.spec.ts` (add skipped mismatch-rejection + constant-time assertions).
- Create/modify: `apps/server/src/app/utils/generate-session-id.function.spec.ts` (add skipped unguessable-derivation assertion).
- No changes to production `.ts` in this story.
